newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-EURO HEROES FALTER AS BREMEN MOVE UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EURO HEROES FALTER AS BREMEN MOVE UP.

text.p: Hamburg and Karlsruhe, Germany's two outstanding sides in the UEFA Cup in midweek, came down to earth with a bump on Saturday as they crashed to Bundesliga defeats.

Karlsruhe, starting the day in fifth place, failed to build on their glittering 3-0 triumph over Roma on Tuesday. In-form Thomas Haesser gave them a first-half lead at home to Werder Bremen but the visitors stepped up a gear to win 3-1.
A goal from Bruno Labbadia sandwiched between strikes from Austrians Heimo Pfeifenberger and Andreas Herzog gave Bremen a comfortable victory and moved them up to fourth place.
"We deserved to win because of our second half performance," said Bremen coach Hans-Juergen "Dixie" Doerner.
"In the first half we defended well but didn't manage to attack enough."

Saturday's results had no effect on the top three placings. VfB Stuttgart and Bayer Leverkusen drew 0-0 on Friday night, leaving them first and second respectively. Third-placed Bayern Munich take on champions Dortmund, lying fifth, on Sunday.

Hamburg, who looked impressive in their 3-0 win over Spartak Moscow on Wednesday, went down to 2-0 away to Schalke to give the home side's Dutch coach Huub Stevens his first Bundesliga win since taking over earlier this month.
"We could have played all day and still not scored," commented Hamburg's disappointed coach Felix Magath.
While the UEFA Cup stars faded, Borussia Moenchengladbach -- the only German side to lose in Europe in midweek -- reversed their fortunes with a 2-0 win over Hansa Rostock.
Thomas Kasternmaeier helped Moenchengladbach to forget their 4-2 drubbing by Monaco with a superb solo effort in the 57th minute and Marco Villa added a header 13 minutes later.
Moenchengladbach coach Bernd Krauss, under pressure after several poor results, was full of praise for 18-year old Villa.
"Even if he hadn't scored a goal today, he'd still have had a very good game," Krauss said.

"I'm really pleased we won such a really important game. After losing to Monaco we wanted to put all our energy into winning this one. Now we have to move up the table," said Krauss, whose side are 10th.
Cologne climbed from eighth to sixth with a 4-1 win over bottom side Arminia Bielefeld.
Despite the presence of Germany striker Stefan Kuntz, Bielefeld remain last, scraping together just seven points from 11 games.
